messages:
zane: Anyone see an odd p99 bump on /internal/checkpoint this morning? p50/p95 fine but p99 doubled around 09:10 UTC.

mei: yep caught that in the daily snapshot. looks concentrated to caller_tag=partner-ingest and sample_origin=worker-retry.

owen: could be retry storm or misattributed retry samples. we shipped an ingress change that renames `x-rw-retry-of` -> `x-retry-parent` last night. telemetry expects the old header.

infra-bot: Alert: p99 for /internal/checkpoint exceeded threshold (baseline 200ms) at 2026-03-17T09:12Z.

lucy: if retries lost their parent id they won't dedupe. that would inflate tail without affecting p50/p95 much. can we check unique request_id counts?

mei: quick query: `SELECT request_id, count(*) FROM telemetry_latency WHERE route='/internal/checkpoint' AND time>now()-interval '30 minutes' GROUP BY request_id ORDER BY count DESC LIMIT 20;` shows multiple request_ids with count>1, but some appear under different header names.

zane: patch idea: add header alias mapping in telemetry-ingest and then backfill 3h of data. also add a dashboard note when aliases are changed so ops know sample provenance changed.

owen: agreed. I'll land alias mapping to canary in 10m and schedule a backfill job. will also add a small flag in the latency panel showing "recent aliasing change" when mappings change.

lucy: please also add a quick unit test to ingest that simulates both header names so we avoid regressions.

mei: filed ticket RT-4410 to track mapping, backfill, dashboard annotation, and tests.

zane: nice. once canary is patched we'll re-evaluate p99 and close the alert if it drops. :thumbsup:
